headline: Comp sales lift revenue as investment gains boost profit
summary_short: Walmart's Q1 FY2027 revenue rose 7.3% y/y to $177,751M on 4.3% Walmart U.S. and 5.9% Sam's Club comparable-sales growth plus 26% eCommerce growth, while net income climbed 18.8% y/y to $5,330M ($0.67 diluted EPS) as other gains/losses swung to a $0.3B net gain from a $0.6B net loss a year ago.
summary_long: Q1 FY2027 net sales rose 7.3% y/y to $177.8B, led by 4.3% Walmart U.S. and 5.9% Sam's Club comparable sales, 26% eCommerce growth, and a $2.3B currency tailwind. Gross margin rose 6bps on mix shift toward higher-margin businesses like advertising, but expenses rose 33bps of sales on depreciation, $0.2B reorganization charges, and healthcare costs, leaving operating income up only 5.0% to $7.49B. Net income jumped 18.8% to $5.33B ($0.67 diluted EPS), boosted by a swing to $0.3B investment gains from $0.6B losses a year ago, despite a higher 23.2% tax rate. Capex rose to $6.68B from $5.0B, pushing free cash flow to negative $1.9B; cash ended at $10.7B, buybacks fell to $2.08B, dividend rose to $0.99/share.

drivers.explanation: Total revenue rose $12.1B (7.3%) on Walmart U.S. comp sales +4.3% and Sam's Club U.S. comp sales +5.9%, eCommerce sales up 26% ($8.5B), and a $2.3B positive currency effect.

Gross margin rose 6bps on mix shift toward higher-margin businesses like advertising, but operating expenses rose 33bps of sales on higher depreciation, $0.2B of Walmart U.S. reorganization charges, and higher associate healthcare costs, netting only a modest operating-income gain.

Net income outgrew operating income as other gains and losses swung to a $0.3B net gain (investment fair-value changes) from a $0.6B net loss a year ago, despite a higher 23.2% effective tax rate versus 22.6%.
Basic EPS growth of 19.6% slightly exceeds net income's 18.8% rise because basic weighted-average shares fell about 0.5% y/y on continued buybacks.
Diluted EPS growth mirrors net income's 18.8% rise, aided by a roughly 0.6% y/y decline in diluted weighted-average shares from continued buybacks.

Operating margin (operating income over total revenue) slipped as opex growth from depreciation, reorganization charges, and healthcare costs outpaced the gross-margin gain; management's own net-sales-basis measure showed a smaller 8bp decline.
Net margin rose because net income grew faster (+18.8%) than revenue (+7.3%), driven mainly by the swing to net investment gains that outweighed the higher effective tax rate.

MD&A frames the quarter under Walmart's 'Growth, Margin, Returns' framework: comparable-sales and eCommerce growth plus margin discipline drove results, with returns funded via capex, dividends, and buybacks. This 10-Q was filed standalone, without an earnings-release exhibit, so no CEO/CFO quote accompanies it.
